Threshold-weighted versions of standard scores stay proper in this setup. The CRPS and log score both adapt cleanly. Quantile and interval forecasts keep local elicitability under the same weights. Mean forecasts do not, they prove. Honest forecast grading must respect the horizon from the start.
arxiv-2603-15235: Zhu and co-authors upgrade the IllustrisTNG galaxy simulation with black hole feedback physics from the MACER model. Standard subgrid feedback in TNG skips recent detail on accretion and outflows. Their hybrid keeps the TNG accretion estimate but adopts MACER rules for feedback at high and low rates. In test ellipticals, star formation and accretion rose, and gas profiles matched observations better. In a full cosmological box, most large-scale outcomes stayed similar. Low-mass black holes in small galaxies improved, though the sharp color split of galaxies faded.
arxiv-2603-15335: Gajewski and co-authors augment data by bootstrapping causal residuals. Standard augmentation edits data points with domain know-how, like tinting an image. Causal knowledge, such as A causes B causes C, can guide richer edits. Their method fits models on marginal distributions, then permutes the residuals between points. This respects the rule that separate mechanisms act on their own. Models trained on the augmented data predict more accurately. Theory backs the gain in linear Gaussian settings, and the approach uses facts beyond a Markov equivalence class.
arxiv-2603-15435: Zoakos studies holographic Krylov complexity on the Coulomb branch of N=4 super Yang-Mills theory. He adopts the view that the growth rate of this complexity mirrors the radial momentum of a heavy probe particle. Two probe paths in the dual geometry get full treatment. One path yields exact formulas, even with extra motion in the inner space. Paths that dodge the inner singularity give an oscillating complexity, set by the Coulomb scale. Paths that near the singularity lose that pattern. Field theory checks agree in broad terms.
arxiv-2603-15535: Sidky and Pan write background notes on the Chambolle-Pock primal-dual algorithm for X-ray tomographic reconstruction. The notes aim at imaging scientists who want intuition, not just formulas. They present the method as an algorithmic system that welcomes pre-conditioning. Essential facts from non-smooth convex analysis are built up inside the text. The goal is a self-contained path from the basics to use on real reconstruction problems.
arxiv-2603-15635: Kim and co-authors join two hard simulation tasks in one variational framework. Phase-field fracture turns sharp cracks into a smooth damage field. Third-medium contact replaces a contact surface with a soft fake medium. Both tricks remove the need for crack tracking or contact search. The team tests two-dimensional bending and a three-dimensional Brazilian disk. The disk test shows crushing zones near contact points, as seen in lab tests.
arxiv-2603-15735: Thoss, Loeb, and Burkert weigh the interstellar visitor 3I/ATLAS from its odd acceleration. The object vented gas and dust near perihelion and brightened fast. Outgassing pushed it off a pure gravity path. The team models water and carbon dioxide loss rates. If carbon dioxide dominates surface loss, the nucleus spans 0.42 km. Its mass then sits near 1.6 times 10^11 kg. Water-led models give larger sizes but clash with the push data. Much water loss likely happens in the coma instead.
arxiv-2603-15935: Sun and co-authors replay a Gerrit-era study of test code review on GitHub. Test code guards product code, yet review habits for it stay little known. Six open-source projects supply the pull request data. GitHub's pull model yields more balanced test and product talk than Gerrit. Overall comment density runs lower in the pull model. GitHub Actions adoption then swung focus hard toward product code. For test-touching requests, review odds and comments hit median zero. They warn that pipeline shifts can starve test review.
arxiv-2603-16035: Shang and Woźniak add flexible switching volatility to structural VAR models. Each shock's variance follows its own Markov chain in their setup. Extra regimes may sit empty across the whole sample. That sparsity keeps the regime count honest and lean. A new distribution for scaled variances eases Gibbs sampling. The model sharpens structural estimates past popular rival forms. Homoskedasticity checks gain a reliable in-model test. Forecast scores match stochastic volatility benchmarks closely. A US monetary shock is identified through volatility shifts.
arxiv-2603-16135: Funano proves two universal bounds for Neumann eigenvalues on convex domains. The Laplacian's Neumann spectrum sets how waves and heat behave in a region. Universal bounds hold for every domain in a class at once. His note targets Euclidean domains with convex shape. Two inequalities tie the Neumann eigenvalues together in that setting. Short notes of this kind give later work firm reference points. Spectral geometry gains two more shape-free constraints.
arxiv-2603-16335: Yap steers the behavior of a 35B mixture-of-experts language model. He trains nine sparse autoencoders on the model's residual stream. Linear probes on the autoencoder features target five agentic traits. Probe weights pass back through the decoder to form steering vectors. Across 1,800 rollouts, autonomy steering flipped the model from asking help to acting alone. Cross-trait checks showed all five vectors move one agency axis. Steering during decoding alone had no effect.
arxiv-2603-16435: Wang and co-authors shrink the key-value cache of large language models. Long contexts swell the cache and strain small machines. Older training-free tricks use low-rank fits or scalar quantization. Those fail to give high compression and high fidelity at once. Their VQKV method applies vector quantization instead. Thousands of values become a few integer indices. On LLaMA3.1-8B it compresses the cache by 82.8% while keeping 98.6% of baseline scores, and allows 4.3 times longer output on the same memory.
arxiv-2603-16535: Stein, Li, and Steidl speed up transformer attention with inertial dynamics. Attention blocks can be read as particle systems. Their mean-field limits are gradient flows on density spaces. The team adds Nesterov-style momentum to that picture. Tokens now carry velocity as well as position. The resulting blocks form Hamiltonian momentum attention. For linear attention, the blocks mimic a Stein flow of an energy. Tests show faster convergence at the same oracle cost.
arxiv-2603-16835: Kröber, Hoxha, and Roscher assess data-centric methods that find wrong labels in remote sensing datasets. Bad labels are common in real data and can badly limit deep learning models. The team tests three methods that flag and isolate noisy labels, not just cope with them. They inject label noise from 10 to 70 percent into two benchmark datasets, in several noise patterns. They track how well each method filters noise and how task scores change. Their results show which method fits which setting, and where more research is needed.
arxiv-2603-16935: Zhang and co-authors present GenLie, a network that detects lies from video under weak and noisy signals. Deceptive cues are subtle and brief, and identity differences add strong noise. GenLie models local features under global supervision. Local modeling catches the sparse cues. Global supervision suppresses identity related noise and keeps the learned features discriminative. The authors test the system on three public datasets. These cover both high stakes and low stakes scenarios. They report that GenLie beats prior state of the art methods on all three.
arxiv-2603-17035: Goettems and co-authors test the dissipative adaptation hypothesis in a quantum system. The hypothesis says self organization grows from a system's skill at dumping absorbed work as heat. They study a driven spin-boson model: a particle in a double well with tunable asymmetry, coupled to a reservoir. Within a path integral formalism, they track how work from the dynamic potential links to the jump probability between the two ground states. Their results motivate deeper study of the model's thermodynamics.
arxiv-2603-17435: Fan and co-authors present ZipServ, a lossless compression system for serving large language models. Older entropy codecs slow GPU inference with ragged bitstreams and extra memory traffic. ZipServ uses a fixed-length bitmap encoding built for tensor cores. A fused kernel decompresses weights straight into compute registers during matrix work. Model size fell by up to 30 percent in their tests. End-to-end inference sped up by 1.22 times on average.
arxiv-2603-17535: Köhler and Breuß ask whether design parameters can be read back from PCA geometry codes. CAD shapes often need many parameters, so PCA shrinks the space to main variation modes. That code is compact but hides the original parameter values. They show a recent field-specific PCA variant matches the standard method exactly. They then give conditions where parameter recovery stays accurate and interpretable. Stage-by-stage tests trace where geometry shifts.
arxiv-2603-17635: Elson and co-authors find a sharp shadow mode inside a two-magnon continuum. Their neutron scattering probes a square-lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet in a copper-organic material. Strong fields past one third of saturation reveal the odd mode. It tracks the one-magnon branches at an offset set by the Larmor energy. Matrix-product-state runs match the spectrum, they report. The mode reads as a bound pair: one magnon locked to uniform precession.
arxiv-2603-17835: Prosen studies a boundary defect in the Heisenberg spin-1/2 chain. The two spins near the edge interact with a strength unlike the bulk. For strong edge coupling, he builds a conserved operator that hugs the boundary. A matrix-product ansatz gives the mode in explicit form. Boundary correlations then refuse to decay, with a nonzero Drude weight, he shows. At a finite critical coupling, the mode's reach diverges and ergodic edge dynamics take over.
arxiv-2603-18135: Eappen and Kroupa introduce a MOND depth index and a dynamical maturity clock for stellar systems. Mass discrepancies appear only below the acceleration scale a0, they note. Their indices track crossing time, relaxation time, and mean acceleration across galaxies and clusters. A clean split emerges: the dark matter effect shows only in deep-MOND, collisionless systems. High-acceleration collisional systems like globular clusters show no discrepancy, giving one scheme for both.
arxiv-2603-18235: Chaturvedi, Bergerson, and Mallick argue for reliable, safe, and secure LLMs in scientific work. LLM agents promise much as AI scientists but bring biosafety and misuse risks. General safety benchmarks miss science-specific threats and suffer domain mismatch, they note. They build a taxonomy of threats for research settings. A multi-agent system could auto-generate domain adversarial benchmarks, feeding a layered defense with a safety agent inside.
arxiv-2603-18535: Kim and co-authors tackle one-handed scaling of 3D objects in extended reality. Standard gaze plus pinch control lets users pick, move, and rotate items with one hand. Scaling still needs two hands. Their Align-to-Scale method uses gaze and hand alignment as a mode switch for pinch-to-scale. They test several variants in a task that mixes moving and scaling. All variants enable one-handed scaling, each with distinct trade-offs. The authors draw design guidelines for future mobile 3D interfaces.
arxiv-2603-19335: Li asks whether the many post-training methods for language models truly differ in effect. A shared testbed, OXRL, runs 51 methods under one setup for fair checks. The study covers eight methods at four model sizes and three test fields. Rankings flip with scale: the worst small-scale method tops the chart at 7 billion weights. Twenty variants of DPO add no real gain over the plain form. Score spreads shrink by over 30 times outside the training field. Scale, the study finds, dwarfs method choice.
arxiv-2603-19535: Traini and co-authors study engagement in SONAR, a virtual reality app for learning sign language. Three measures were tracked: visual attention, video replay frequency, and post-playback viewing time. Learners trained at their own pace, then took a validation quiz. Visual attention correlated strongly with quiz scores, and viewing time also helped. Replay frequency showed no real link to success. Attention traces peaked at dense segments of the videos. The results stress steady, well-placed attention in immersive learning.
arxiv-2603-19835: Ma and co-authors present FIPO, a reinforcement learning method for deep reasoning in language models. Standard GRPO-style training spreads one outcome reward over every token. That coarse credit cannot tell key logic steps from filler tokens. FIPO adds discounted future-KL terms into the policy update. Tokens are weighted by their sway over what follows. On Qwen2.5-32B, chains of thought grew from about 4,000 to over 10,000 tokens. AIME 2024 accuracy rose from 50.0 to a peak of 58.0 percent. That beat DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Math-32B and roughly matched o1-mini.
arxiv-2603-19935: Borro and co-authors present Memori, a persistent memory layer for agents built on large language models. Raw chat history stuffed into prompts costs many tokens and hurts performance. Memori instead turns dialogue into compact semantic triples and short summaries. That structure supports precise retrieval across sessions and across models. On the LoCoMo benchmark it reached 81.95 percent accuracy. It used only 1,294 tokens per query, about 5 percent of full context. The authors argue structured memory beats simply enlarging context windows.
arxiv-2603-20035: Mukherjee designs a quantum key distribution protocol that leans on full network nonlocality. This stronger form of network quantumness cannot arise in standard Bell tests. The protocol serves four parties linked by entangled sources. Its security rests on spotting full network nonlocality through a trilocal inequality. Mukherjee sorts two-qubit states by error rate and inequality violation to judge their use. She also gauges an eavesdropper's partial side information in a restricted setting. The key rate is discussed, plus resistance to the detection loophole.
arxiv-2603-20135: Hsu and Shekhar build sequential tests that learn their rules from a trained classifier. The null and rival classes are known only through offline sample data. A fresh stream of unlabeled data then arrives, one point at a time. Their test reaches a level alpha, power one decision using a multi class classifier. Under a mild separability condition, they bound the expected stopping time. That bound cannot be improved in general. The procedure can also name the true source distribution almost surely.
arxiv-2603-20535: Beerbower and co-authors introduce Lehmer parking functions and count their outcomes. Parking functions are a classic combinatorial object with rich structure. Their Lehmer variant comes with a defined set of parking outcomes. The number of outcomes equals a Bell number, they prove. That is exactly the count of set partitions of an n-element set. For weakly decreasing Lehmer parking functions, the count is a Catalan number. Those outcomes match the non-intersecting set partitions. The results link a new parking family to two famous sequences.
arxiv-2603-20935: Zuyev and Benner study periodic solutions of nonlinear control systems with bang-bang switching controls. Such systems arise in periodic optimal control with bounded inputs, for example in chemical reaction tuning. They turn the search for a periodic solution into a fixed point problem for composed exponential maps. The Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff-Dynkin formula then links these solutions to an autonomous system built from Lie brackets. Stability arguments reduce the task further, to finding equilibria of that system. They apply the theory to nonlinear chemical reaction models with constrained controls.
arxiv-2603-21135: Tseng and co-authors replace the single memory pool in test-time adaptation with a multi-cluster memory. Test-time adaptation tunes a pretrained model on unlabeled test data as it arrives. Under realistic streams, the data is time correlated and multi-modal, so one pool fits poorly. Their MCM framework sorts stored samples into clusters by light pixel level descriptors. Neighboring clusters merge to bound memory size, and retrieval balances supervision across modes. Added to three adaptation methods, it improves all twelve test setups.
arxiv-2603-21235: Hirose and Rodola propose Domain Elastic Transform, a grid-free Bayesian method for registering functions on irregular domains. Standard registration splits into point set methods for sparse shapes and image methods for grid data. New data, such as spatial transcriptomics, holds high dimensional signals on sparse supports, so neither fits well. Their method aligns geometry and function jointly, with no binning. On mouse brain and embryo data, it gives strong spatial overlap and topology among tested pipelines.
arxiv-2603-21335: Vinjamuri and co-authors build TimeTox, a pipeline that extracts time toxicity from clinical trial protocols. Time toxicity counts the health care contact days that trial participation demands from a patient. The pipeline uses Gemini models in three stages. First it extracts summaries from protocol PDFs. Then it counts contact days at six timepoints for each treatment arm. Last, it builds consensus across runs. On six hundred forty four real oncology protocols, a single pass design proves more reproducible than a two stage design.
arxiv-2603-21435: Park studies a governance problem that arises when organizations buy AI decision support. Vendors bake value judgments into these systems, and buyers cannot see or renegotiate them. Park defines the behavioural feasible set: the recommendations a system can actually reach under vendor-set alignment constraints. Experiments with binary choices and multi-stakeholder rankings show alignment shrinks that set a lot. Aligned systems resist even fair contextual pressure, and they shift which stakeholders get priority instead of staying neutral.
arxiv-2603-21535: Kawalec derives a series expansion for the prime zeta function around its logarithmic singularity at s equals 1. He proves a general formula for the expansion coefficients, in the spirit of the Stieltjes constants for the Riemann zeta function. The results can also be read as a higher-order generalization of Mertens's theorems. Kawalec checks the formulas numerically to high precision on several test cases. The work ties a classic function of prime number theory to a cleaner coefficient structure.
arxiv-2603-22235: Watkin and co-authors rework decision boundary maps, a tool for viewing how classifiers split data. Map quality depends heavily on the dimensionality reduction behind it. In raw data space, classes often mix and the maps mislead. Their method first moves data into Shapley space. It then runs the reduction on those Shapley values. The resulting maps show tighter, easier zones to explore. Quality scores match or beat maps built from raw data. The zones also agree better with measured model performance.
arxiv-2603-22335: Zhao and co-authors fix a flaw in preference tuning for generative recommenders. Direct Preference Optimization aligns model output with past user behavior. The authors show it also amplifies spurious links set by hidden confounders. That harms performance when the data distribution shifts. Their fix, CausalDPO, adds a causal invariance mechanism to the tuning step. It adjusts for confounders with a backdoor strategy. It also models the hidden environment mix by soft clustering. Across four shift settings, they report gains near 17 percent on average.
arxiv-2603-22435: Fu and co-authors present CaP-X, an open framework for studying coding agents that control robots. Inside it, CaP-Gym lets agents write and run programs that combine perception and control steps. Their CaP-Bench tests twelve frontier models at varied levels of abstraction and grounding. Scores rise with hand-crafted aids but fall as those aids are removed. The team shows that more test-time interaction and feedback can close much of the gap. Their CaP-Agent0 then matches human-level reliability on several tasks.
arxiv-2603-22535: Dang and co-authors validate and extend SCALE-Sim, a cycle-level simulator for TPU-style accelerators. Simulators often drift from real hardware, so the team checks its core matrix model against a Google TPU v4. Simulated cycles track measured latency closely enough for a simple conversion. They add small learned models for non-matrix operations, cutting end-to-end timing errors sharply. A new frontend based on StableHLO lets workloads flow in straight from JAX and PyTorch. The result is a more faithful tool for whole-model timing studies.
arxiv-2603-22635: Quaglio-Gomes and co-authors probe how electric pulses move oxygen vacancies in YBCO devices. YBCO is a high-temperature superconductor, and vacancy control could tune its behavior. The team combines several X-ray methods with transport and optical tests. The results show the crystal's c-axis grows as oxygen leaves the copper-oxygen chains. Maps of that growth match the optical contrast seen after migration. The authors also warn that optical images alone can miss strong resistance changes. Their work links surface signs to deeper oxygen shifts.
arxiv-2603-22735: Chan, Zhao, and Gaizauskas set a new task for language models: explaining away apparent contradictions. Most work treats contradictions as errors to settle by picking a winner. Human reasoners instead often invent a story that makes both claims fit. The authors reuse inference datasets to build the task and its quality metrics. Tests on 13 models show limited success. Longer reasoning chains link to worse results, not better. A training proof of concept improves accuracy on two story reasoning benchmarks in non-thinking mode.
arxiv-2603-22935: Zhang and co-authors build the Ran Score, a metric for grading chest X-ray reports. Auto-generated reports often miss rare findings and mishandle negation. Their framework pairs clinician guidance with language models to extract findings from free text. Ran Score then grades reports finding by finding. Prompt tuning lifts agreement with radiologist labels sharply on MIMIC data. The score beats the CheXbert benchmark on shared labels by a wide margin. A Chinese validation cohort shows the method generalizes well.
arxiv-2603-23035: Latorre and Segura de León study a total variation flow equation with rough data. The Dirichlet problem is driven by the 1-Laplacian operator. Data have minimal integrability: the source and start values sit in L1 spaces. The authors prove existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions. Their proof uses an approximation scheme and an entropy form fit to the operator. Added results cover solution comparison and better regularity for nicer data. Long-time decay is analyzed for the homogeneous case.
arxiv-2603-23335: Cuddy and four co-authors study how a weak coronal shock sped up particles on 10 March 2024. Global EUV waves can act as shocks, and their punch depends on local plasma traits. The team mixes EUV images with radio imaging and spectra to locate the boost. Radio herringbone patterns point to electron beams inside a dimming region as the wave passed. Drift rates put those electrons at 75 to 122 keV. The shock was barely supersonic, with Mach near 1.005. Field geometry, they argue, decides where acceleration can happen.
arxiv-2603-23635: Basar, Pradeep, and Stephanov constrain proton burst patterns near the QCD critical point. Heavy-ion hunts for that point read the peaks and dips of proton counts. Their method leans on the shape of the QCD equation of state near the point. Lee-Yang singularity data, drawn from lattice work by Padé resummation, bind the cumulant curves. Four distinct stories fit inside the error bars. Each story sets the point's spot and the crossover slope apart. The third cumulant splits the stories most clearly for lab tests.
arxiv-2603-23735: Leroux and seven co-authors watch active matter organize itself on a closed curved skin. Their lab system coats oil droplets with microtubules driven by kinesin motors. The sphere's shape forces a total defect charge that four half-defects carry. Those defects swing in steady cycles between flat and tetrahedral layouts. Starving the coat of filaments loosens the dance into a wilder, reversing regime. Squeezing a droplet bends its curve map and spawns fresh defects. Shape, density, and motion alone grow the cycles.
arxiv-2603-23835: Ghosal and co-authors build inference theory for deep neural network versions of the Cox survival model. Key gaps concern how training error affects risk, and how to control bias for valid tests. They prove oracle bounds that link training error to population risk for general trained networks. A structured network design then keeps pointwise bias small. With ensemble subsampling, they prove normal limits and give a jackknife form for the covariance. Simulations and a real dataset show the theory at work.
arxiv-2603-24035: Asthana and co-authors present Clifford lensing, a way to focus phase information in large quantum systems. In many-body systems, interactions spread phase data across many degrees of freedom, which hides it from easy measurements. Clifford operations on states and observables can refocus that spread onto fewer qubits. The authors link this trick to quantum error-correcting codes and deterministic phase kickback. They also give partial shadow tomography protocols for subsystem phases. NMR tests with up to fifteen qubits show optimal sensing with limited resources.
arxiv-2603-24235: Zenin and co-authors check early-universe scenarios in a non-minimal effective scalar-tensor gravity theory. They study whether bounce, inflation, and genesis stages can all work inside this framework. Each stage is supported, they find. Accelerated expansion comes from the theory's own degrees of freedom, not from added matter. The theory also gives two different values of the Hubble parameter. That could match the different Hubble constant values read from galaxy clusters and from relic radiation, they suggest.
arxiv-2603-24335: Morisco argues that generative AI creates a new form of informational inequality. The knowledge gap view says new information tends to widen social gaps. Digital divide research added gaps in access and in use of technology. Morisco shifts the focus to evaluation. People with more education are more likely, he assumes, to question and contextualize AI output. People with less education may accept it more directly. He presents this as a conceptual framework, with no new empirical findings, meant to guide future research on education and AI.
arxiv-2603-24835: Ouyang and co-authors present DCARL, a divide-and-conquer framework for long video generation. Video diffusion models scale poorly to long sequences, while autoregressive models drift. A keyframe generator, trained without temporal compression, first sets global structural anchors. An interpolation generator then fills dense frames in overlapping segments, using keyframes for global context and one clean prior frame. Trained on a large internet dataset, the method beats rivals on visual quality and camera adherence.
arxiv-2603-24935: Wu and co-authors present SABER, a stealthy black-box attack framework for robot models. Small text edits to an instruction can change robot behaviour, so robustness testing needs an automatic attacker. SABER trains a ReAct-style attacker with reinforcement learning to craft small edits under a bounded budget. Its tools work at character, token, and prompt level. On the LIBERO benchmark across six models, task success falls by 20.6 percent, action sequences grow by 55 percent, and constraint violations rise by 33 percent.
arxiv-2603-25035: Elluru and co-authors ask what model compression does inside vision-language models. Shops shrink these models by pruning or quantization to save memory and compute. The team uses causal circuit tracing and feature matching to compare the two. Pruning mostly keeps the circuit layout but twists and weakens features. Quantization changes circuits more, yet the features that survive stay better aligned. They also release VLMSafe-420, a test set pairing harmful prompts with matched safe twins. Pruning sharply cuts true refusal behavior, so the choice of method carries safety weight.
arxiv-2603-25235: Brooks and co-authors infer how fast a disease spreads inside homes when the home layout itself is hidden. Final-size data say who fell ill, but not how homes were structured. The spread rate that modelers need hides behind that missing structure. Their Bayesian method fills in plausible household layouts as it samples, using a Markov chain search. It works at several reporting resolutions. On fake data it covers the true rate over 90 percent of the time. A COVID-19 dataset shows size-split reporting cuts error a lot.
arxiv-2603-25535: Brunner and co-authors learn how to paint back marks that a camera system can tell apart on look-alike pigs. Farms want per-animal tracking, but uniform species give few natural clues. A ResNet-50 network learned to name ten pigs by their back marks. Studying its hits and misses shows which design choices matter. Each mark must stay clear under motion blur, odd angles, and bodies blocking the view. The rules can guide marking plans for future trials and working farms.
arxiv-2603-25635: De Villeroché and co-authors present AB-SWIFT, a transformer model that predicts steady air flow in cities. Full fluid dynamics runs are costly, and learned models struggle with varied city shapes and large meshes. AB-SWIFT uses a branched structure built for this task. It trains on simulations around randomized urban layouts. The training set mixes unstable, neutral, and stable air conditions. The authors report the best accuracy on all predicted fields among the models they compare. Code and data are public.
arxiv-2603-25735: Montefalcone and Stiskalek propose a new two-parameter way to describe dark energy. Standard practice uses the CPL form, which tracks the equation of state. Their form instead tracks the dark energy density itself, scaled to its value today. The two parameters are the density and the equation of state at one pivot redshift. They test it with DESI data, Planck priors, and supernova samples. Both parameters are tightly bounded, they report. The values sit close to the cosmological constant case. Evidence for evolving dark energy stays below three sigma.
arxiv-2603-26235: Alex and co-authors present GS-BrainText, a dataset of 8,511 brain scan reports from the Generation Scotland cohort. Of these, 2,431 reports carry expert labels for 24 brain disease types. The reports come from five Scottish NHS health boards, with a mean patient age of 58. A test with the EdIE-R rule-based tool shows scores vary by board, disease type, and age group. The team offers the data to help build clinical text tools that work across sites.
arxiv-2603-26435: Tran and co-authors propose Wattchmen, a method to measure and predict GPU energy use in fine detail. Big GPU clusters face tight energy limits, but current attribution tools are rough or stale. Wattchmen builds a per-instruction energy model from a wide set of microbenchmarks. Across 16 workloads it cuts mean error to 14% on V100 chips, beating prior tools at 32% and 25%. It holds up on A100 and H100 chips too, and its insights cut energy use by up to 35%.
arxiv-2603-26635: Milkowski and Weninger study deception among language model agents playing the social deduction game Among Us. Across 1,100 games, the agents produced over a million tokens of meeting dialogue. Speech act analysis shows all agents lean on directive language most of the time. Impostor agents shift slightly toward explanations and denials when they speak. Deception mostly takes the form of equivocation rather than outright lies, and it grows under social pressure. It rarely lifts win rates, exposing a tension between honesty and utility.
arxiv-2603-27235: Parra and co-authors report narrow X-ray emission lines from the black hole candidate MAXI J1744-294. Such lines are rare in black hole binaries and usually appear in obscured states. This source was caught in a bright soft state. Modeling out neighboring sources left a static, narrow emission component intrinsic to the system. It likely comes from a highly ionized plasma in the inner disk atmosphere. Extra features between 6.7 and 7.1 keV match no rest-frame transitions. Blueshifted iron lines from fast outflows are the favored explanation.
arxiv-2603-27335: Zhang and co-authors present PubMed Reasoner, a biomedical question answering agent that grounds answers in retrieved evidence. A self-critic first refines the query by checking MeSH term coverage and redundancy. Reflective retrieval then reads article batches until the evidence suffices. Final answers carry explicit citations to the gathered sources. With a GPT-4o backbone, the system scored 78.32 percent on PubMedQA. That slightly surpassed human expert performance on the benchmark. Judge evaluations also preferred its answers for grounding and trustworthiness. The design controls compute and token costs throughout.
arxiv-2603-27435: Zhao and co-authors try to improve long AI-written reports by teaching intent. Good reports rest on reasons to write and cite each part. Models rarely see those reasons in training. The team uses tag schemes to pull hidden intents from text. Those tags boost report quality in zero-shot use. They also yield training data for smaller models. Large models gain about three points on hard tasks. Small models gain over twelve points. Citation use and readability both improve.
arxiv-2603-27635: Chitu and co-authors bound the size of digit-restricted number sets. They study irrational numbers written in N-expansions. One set caps all digits at a fixed bound. Its Hausdorff dimension gets sharp Jarník-type bounds. Those bounds refine classic continued fraction results. A second set lets digits grow without bound. Its dimension proves to be exactly one half. Sets with large digits approach that value slowly. Log decay rates are given in full.
arxiv-2603-27735: Ayoola and co-authors map how software teams can act for social good. Social sustainability in software lacks a firm base. Speed and profit often push it aside. A narrative review gathers past definitions. Key facets include equity, well-being, and community cohesion. Measurement and uptake challenges get close analysis. A fresh definition of the concept follows. A roadmap then guides practice and study.
arxiv-2603-27835: Bandelt and co-authors study the geometry of ample, or lopsided, sets. Such sets encode how a convex body meets the orthants. They arise in Lawrence's 1983 work and Dress's later work. Realizations as cubihedra give fresh characterizations. With the intrinsic l1 metric, these shapes match isometric subspaces. Face barycenter maps act like sign vectors. Links to oriented matroid covectors appear as well.
arxiv-2603-28135: Ma and eight co-authors present CoT2-Meta, a framework that adds metacognitive control to test-time reasoning. Most methods just sample more chains or search bigger trees, with no control over when to expand, prune, fix, or stop. CoT2-Meta pairs chain-of-thought generation with a meta-controller and a step-level scoring oracle. Under matched compute budgets it beat sampling and search baselines on six tests, including MATH and GSM8K. Gains held across a wider 15-benchmark suite.
arxiv-2603-28335: Torralba and co-authors report a black hole star at cosmic noon, a Little Red Dot galaxy with an extreme Balmer break at redshift 1.73. Such dots were known mostly at earlier times, and few appear this late. Webb imaging found the object, and deep VLT spectra confirmed it. Its light fits a cool photosphere near 4,800 K, and its hydrogen line shows deep absorption from fast, thick winds. A host galaxy of about a hundred million solar masses surrounds it.
arxiv-2603-28535: Carrasco and Rodriguez-Hertz give a new proof of a Burger-Monod theorem in bounded cohomology, using thermodynamic formalism. The setting is a uniform lattice inside a higher-rank semisimple Lie group. The claim: every quasimorphism from the lattice into a Euclidean space, twisted by an orthogonal action, stays bounded. Boundedness forces such maps to be trivial in the bounded sense. The new route ties group cohomology to tools from dynamical systems.
arxiv-2603-28935: Alexander and co-authors introduce Albert, an AI framework that discovers particle physics theories from experimental data. The search for physics beyond the Standard Model faces a vast space of possible theories. Albert encodes the field as a formal language with a rule based grammar. A reinforcement learning setup enforces theory constraints and scores observables against data. Trained only on legacy LEP data, a small transformer rediscovered the Standard Model. It also inferred the top quark and predicted its mass near the measured value.
arxiv-2603-29035: Pinheiro finds a class of non-Hermitian causal processes whose time patterns escape spectral analysis. A model with a strictly causal memory kernel drives the work. Time asymmetric stochastic processes yield sharp transitions at set scales. Those transitions appear as local structures in similarity space but leave no trace in power spectra. The model predicts an asymmetric profile set by an orientation term. It matches high precision counting experiments at very high significance. The results mark a basic limit of spectral analysis for non-stationary processes.
arxiv-2603-29135: Chowdhury and co-authors add quality control to active learning for autonomous microscopy. Self-driving labs can waste effort on noisy, low-quality data. Their framework pairs curiosity-driven sampling with a physics-based filter. The filter fits a simple harmonic oscillator model to each candidate measurement. Poor measurements are excluded during data collection. Tests used spectroscopy data from lead titanate thin films with local noise. The method beat random sampling and standard active learning. It also ran live on a second film sample.
arxiv-2603-29235: Zheng and co-authors present SysOM-AI, a system for diagnosing slowdowns in production AI training. Small operating-system issues can cascade into GPU and network delays. Older profilers watch one layer at a time or add heavy overhead. SysOM-AI traces CPU stacks, GPU kernels, and network events together. It uses eBPF tracing with under 0.4 percent overhead. At Alibaba it ran on over 80,000 GPUs for a year. It helped confirm 94 production issues. Median diagnosis time fell to about ten minutes.
arxiv-2603-29435: Accadia and co-authors give a new proof of Bessenrodt's result on plane partitions. The result links generating series for reversed and skew plane partitions. Geometric wall-crossing formulas for local curves motivated the work. Their proof also recovers a result of Sagan. They add new closed formulas for weighted counts of these partitions. One formula is dual to a theorem by Gansner. Another identity counts hooks of a Young diagram. They restate the results in Fock space language.
arxiv-2603-29535: Vajrala and co-authors present QUAD, a way to run many generative vision tasks on edge devices with one model. Phones now edit images and remove objects with large vision models. Each task adapter used to need its own compiled model copy. That wastes storage and slows run time. Their system feeds adapter weights in at run time instead. Tasks switch without recompiling. A training method aligns all adapters under one shared quantization profile. Tests across chipsets cut memory up to sixfold.
arxiv-2603-30035: Tsai and Tran test NeuralUCB for routing queries among language models by cost and reward. Supervised routers adapt poorly, while partial-feedback methods trade efficiency for flexibility. Their bandit policy learns from reward signals in a simulated online setting. On RouterBench, it beats random and cheapest-first baselines on utility. Against a max-quality reference, it costs far less while staying competitive. The authors flag action discrimination and exploration as open challenges.
arxiv-2604-00035: Chongder presents QR-SPPS, a quantum pipeline for retail supply chain risk simulation. Classical models treat node failures as independent events. At 40 nodes, exact simulation demands 17.6 TB and over 369,000 hours. The pipeline encodes a 40-node retail network as a 40-qubit Ising Hamiltonian, where ZZ coupling terms encode linked cascade chances. A VQE circuit locates the ground-state stress pattern with zero error, detecting failures in 14 of 40 nodes. ADAPT-VQE screening ranks six crisis interventions in constant evaluations per policy, a 287 times speedup, and Density-of-States QPE reconstructs the eigenspectrum.
arxiv-2604-00335: Transfer systems encode commutative structures from equivariant homotopy theory in combinatorial form. They pair additive transfers with multiplicative norms, the two halves of a ring-type structure. DeMark and colleagues give explicit formulas for the largest transfer system that fits with any given additive one. The formulas get simpler for disklike systems, which most often encode additive structures. The team also shows that this compatibility respects inflation from group quotients, so maximal systems can be built up from connected ones.
arxiv-2604-00735: Albrecht and colleagues study combined LHCb and Belle II data on decays of B mesons to D mesons, tau leptons, and neutrinos. Their goal is tighter limits on new physics. Detector runs built on Standard Model ideas can bias the fitted Wilson coefficients, and shared hadronic inputs link analyses across tests. Using event-by-event reweighting instead of repeated large runs, they show a joint fit cuts such biases and sharpens results over separate fits.
arxiv-2604-01035: Aoki, Roest, and Werth spot bispectrum marks from a tachyonic flare of entropy ripples during inflation. Working exactly at the ripple level, they split light and heavy cases. Light masses near the Hubble scale yield the first such bispectrum result, with shared folded-shape boost plus non-smooth squeezed-limit scaling. Heavy masses well above the Hubble scale link boosted folded shapes to a tachyonic echo in squeezed limits. No single-field working description captures the bispectrum for all setups, and they offer shape patterns for cosmic surveys.
arxiv-2604-01735: López and colleagues propose a method for tracing pandemic data correlations across regions, using tools for non-stationary time series, the norm in pandemic records. Unlike classic epidemiological work centered on medical modeling during a pandemic, their approach looks back after the fact. It traces how lockdowns, travel limits, mobility shifts and vaccination drives show up in regions' behavior. The method reads societal responses from collective patterns rather than case counts alone. Its insights can shape future public health plans and show how spread and control interact.
arxiv-2604-02035: Zhao, Tse and Zheng treat speculative trading as an exploratory reinforcement learning problem over entry and exit times. Relaxing stopping times to Cox process jumps with entropy regularized controls yields exploratory Hamilton Jacobi Bellman equations and closed form Gibbs policies. They bound the error and prove convergence to the original problem value, then build an algorithm and demo it on pairs trading. The framework handles general utilities and price processes without fixing a trading rule in advance.
arxiv-2604-02235: Chen and colleagues break the quadratic time barrier for approximate counting in spin systems. Standard counting to sampling reductions run in quadratic time. Their new algorithms run subquadratically across many settings, including the hardcore model of weighted independent sets and the Ising model. The key link is perfect marginal sampling. For two spin systems, a perfect marginal sampler directly yields a fast counting algorithm. For general spin systems, adapted samplers yield low variance estimators in sublinear time.
arxiv-2604-02535: Huang and three colleagues introduce SDMP, a nonlinear method for shrinking high-dimensional data to fewer dimensions, built on an explicit spectral split. Each new dimension is written as a weighted mix of Laplacian eigenvectors from a neighbor graph, with weights learned by a UMAP-style goal. Expanding the spectral subspace step by step makes the trade-off between global layout and local detail visible and controllable, and tests show strong structure preservation.
arxiv-2604-02635: Jin, You and Jing unify classical and quantum control of continuous-variable systems through ancillary pictures on differential manifolds. The two control styles look far apart at first glance. The paper shows one math frame covers both tool sets. Classical helper variables act as invariants that do not change, guiding nonadiabatic passage through phase space, and quantizing the Liouville equation gives Heisenberg motion for ancillary operators. The theory yields single-mode squeezed states near 29.3 decibels and double-mode states near 20.6 decibels.
arxiv-2604-03135: Smolić and colleagues describe a case study where coding models first wrote unit tests for a prototype codebase, then refactored it under those tests. The workflow produced nearly 16,000 lines of tests in hours, reached up to 78 percent branch coverage in key modules, and cut regression risk during large-scale changes. They also note where manual fixes were needed and where model judgment drifted from developer intent.
arxiv-2604-03535: Morell and colleagues extend regression discontinuity analysis with latent variables to layered education data, where students nest within classrooms or schools. They cover designs where treatment is assigned to whole clusters. Multisite designs assign it to single students within clusters. Monte Carlo tests show average treatment effects recover given enough cluster-level sample sizes, including estimates beyond the cutoff.
arxiv-2604-03735: Stephen Arndt and colleagues gave the first fast algorithms for coloring matroid intersections, where a shared ground set must be split into groups that are independent in every matroid. Earlier bounds on how many colors suffice were not constructive, leaning on topological tools. For two matroids they matched the known bound with a 2-approximation, and for k matroids they reached a bound that depends only on k. A new flexible decomposition drives the method, plus a randomized scheme for large chromatic numbers.
arxiv-2604-03835: Alexey Burov and Alexei Tsvelik argued that life-permitting physics is overdetermined, with more fine-tuning constraints than free parameters in the chemical sector. Life's conditions thus rest not only on tuned constants but on a very special form of the laws themselves. Echoing Wigner's 1960 essay on mathematics in science, the paper points to a second marvel: the laws' structure itself seems arranged to permit life.
arxiv-2604-04135: Shuhong Liu and team reviewed the NTIRE 2026 3D Restoration and Reconstruction challenge, built around the RealX3D benchmark of low-light and smoke-degraded scenes. Of 279 registered participants, 33 teams submitted valid results, which the review evaluates against state-of-the-art baselines. Top methods showed significant progress in rebuilding 3D scenes under adverse real-world conditions. The paper draws out shared design principles among the leaders and lessons for handling degraded 3D scenes.
arxiv-2604-04435: Yokoi, Endo and Saito extend neural-network quantum states from many-body problems to strongly interacting few-body problems in continuous space. Using a fully connected feedforward network with Jacobi coordinates, plus a projection method, they compute ground and first excited states for three- to six-body systems of bosons at unitarity. They also treat a mass-imbalanced fermionic system of two identical fermions and a third particle. The approach also reproduces key Efimov features: discrete scale invariance, the wave function's geometric structure, and critical-mass behavior in imbalanced systems.
arxiv-2604-04935: Jiao, Luo, and Zhou prove large deviation bounds for noncommutative random values, extending classic probability results to a quantum-style setting. For the independent case, they link full exponential integrability to large deviation bounds. For martingale differences in this setting, they prove two deviation bounds, one from that integrability and one from Lp bounds. Finally, they prove a version of Gordin's decomposition for this setting. That decomposition lets them derive an ergodic theorem through deviation bounds for such martingales.
arxiv-2604-05035: Choksi and three co-authors explore a two-stage disruption of resonant chains of super-Earths, after TESS finds around young stars. Observations suggest close planets were born in resonance chains that break on a timescale near 100 million years. That timing surprises, because the dissipative forces that capture planets into resonance should keep their orbits stable. First, some mechanism excites free eccentricities, and any seeding of eccentricities of a few percent triggers a second stage of instability on a similar timescale.
arxiv-2604-05435: Dasula and four colleagues check hospital discharge notes by machine, since gaps in these notes split care and send patients back to hospital. They turn the DISCHARGED guide into a 46-question checklist and test 11 language models on 50 notes from the MIMIC-IV base, scored by doctors. Mean scores run from about 55 to 74 percent, and top models match doctors only fairly well, missing vague notes most.
arxiv-2604-05535: Lei and three colleagues evolve readable traffic-signal strategies with language models instead of opaque neural policies or rigid program languages. Each SignalClaw skill carries rationale, selection guidance, and runnable code, refined by simulation feedback and composed by an event dispatcher for emergencies and transit priority. In SUMO tests it nearly matches the best routine delays and beats MaxPressure and DQN sharply on emergency and transit delays.
arxiv-2604-05835: Antognolli and Petrillo lift proofs of concept from casual trials to first-class tools for architectural decisions. A systematic review of research and grey literature yields a refined definition plus a light three-phase frame: planning, execution, and decision-making. They also name the Undocumented Architectural Experiment anti-pattern, where PoCs steer big calls without leaving durable knowledge.
arxiv-2604-05935: Hernandez Acosta and eight colleagues model X-ray Thomson scattering by drawing single scatter events, particle-physics style, rather than fitting full spectra first. Draws from cross-section odds pass through spectrometer runs, keeping full motion detail with bendy setup-aware checks. A fake non-resonant test proves the route works and stays true while cutting repeat-run costs.
arxiv-2604-06135: Kyriacou and three colleagues load data into quantum neural networks by spreading measurement shots across several starting quantum states. The spread follows a classical distribution set by the data, and the shot counts can be learned, giving a mixed-state encoding whose averages combine linearly with nonlinear activations. The design matches a multilayer perceptron whose weights live in quantum circuits. On three image sets it reaches about 89 percent on Semeion, 81 percent on Fashion MNIST, and 90 percent on MNIST, with no data-encoding gates.
arxiv-2604-06435: Barusco and four colleagues benchmark visual anomaly detection for edge devices with tight limits and continual learning, where models learn new data without forgetting skills. Either limit misleads, since methods built for one setting break under the other. Their benchmark, the first edge continual one, weighs seven models on three backbones across memory, inference cost, and quality. They offer Tiny-Dinomaly, a Dinomaly variant on DINO foundation model that cuts memory 11-fold and cost 20-fold while lifting pixel localization by 5 points, plus PatchCore and PaDiM variants.
arxiv-2604-06535: Hatta and five colleagues calculate how the Sun's gravity modes would ripple its neutrino output. Their model of a vibrating spherical star finds the first-order ripple cancels out. A tiny time-varying signal remains, far below present detectors' reach, plus a steadier rise in average flux. Because that rise tracks the Sun's magnetic cycle over roughly eleven years, long-term neutrino records might reveal whole groups of gravity modes and test ideas about what excites them.
arxiv-2604-06735: Liu, Kitaev, and Zhang enumerate ascent sequences avoiding length-four patterns. Ascent sequences link to (2+2)-free posets, Stoimenow matchings, and other Fishburn objects, counted by the Fishburn numbers. The authors count sequences avoiding any subset of the five patterns 0101, 0102, 0112, 0120, and 0121, except the sets 0120 alone, 0121 alone, and the pair together, where counting stays open. Avoidance classes fall into 16 Wilf equivalence classes, touching Catalan and Fibonacci numbers and polynomial and rational formulas, with several sequences apparently new.
arxiv-2604-07035: Manik and Wang evaluate seven reasoning models across four benchmarks. Mixed samples and partial standardization complicate reasoning model selection. The team tests zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and few-shot chain-of-thought prompting on the 238-example subset. It covers 84 conditions. They also report latency, memory, and performance. Gemma-4-26B-A4B with zero-shot scores highest at about 79 percent, while Gemma-4-E4B stays near top with lower latency and memory. A selector reaches about 83 percent, and prompting changes rankings rather than shifting models.
arxiv-2604-07235: Karaev, Blumenthal, and Hacohen-Gourgy give a light-calibration recipe for making Fock states and swapping modes in bosonic quantum computing. A Rabi drive on a weakly coupled transmon plus one sideband tone per mode creates a Jaynes-Cummings link on demand. Every pulse time then follows a simple square-root rule, so no per-state retuning is needed. On a superconducting cavity with two high-quality modes, they make Fock states through five photons, do a mode swap, and swap a dual-rail Bell state with coherence intact.
arxiv-2604-07635: Thakur proposes VREML, a scalable inference method for spatial data with Gaussian ICAR structure. Old likelihood needs repeated inversion of large, sparse precision matrices, which is costly. VREML approximates the hard marginal likelihood with a Gaussian spread and builds an evidence lower bound on the restricted fit. A coordinate-ascent algorithm then estimates spatial random effects and variance parts. The author proves steady convergence and shows the family is exact under ICAR settings, so posterior error vanishes. In tests, the method beats maximum likelihood and INLA.
arxiv-2604-07935: Geens and three colleagues say state-space models traded edge efficiency for cloud throughput, a pattern they call the Hyperscale Lottery. The older Hardware Lottery says research follows available silicon; here, architectures chase hyperscale GPU saturation. Mamba models were praised for linear complexity suited to edge use, yet Mamba-3's changes impose a steep edge penalty. Latency rises 28 percent at 880 million parameters and worsens to 48 percent for 15 million parameter models. The authors urge separating cloud saturation tricks from core design to keep single-user real-time edge use viable.
arxiv-2604-08435: Chen and three colleagues tackle driver fatigue detection from long untrimmed cabin videos under tight computing limits. Their HST-HGN network fuses pose separated face geometry with texture patches through a layered hypergraph, capturing joint facial changes that pairwise graphs miss. A bidirectional state space module then tracks behavior over time, telling yawning from speaking, and the system leads fatigue benchmarks while staying light enough for in car edge use.
arxiv-2604-09035: Foffano and four colleagues present Advantage-Guided Diffusion for model-based reinforcement learning, steering a diffusion model by the agent's edge estimate. Step-by-step world models suffer growing errors, while diffusion models ease the problem by making segments jointly. Older diffusion guides use policy alone, dropping value information, or rewards, which turn myopic over short spans. The guide needs no change to the training goal. On MuJoCo tasks, it lifts sample efficiency and return over a Diffuser-style method and model-free baselines, in some cases by twofold.
arxiv-2604-09335: Santamaria, Soleymani, Gutierrez, and Jorswieck present a simple approach to BD reconfigurable smart panel design in MIMO systems. Such panels improve radio gains through tunable links, but design relied on complex repeat methods. Instead of raising rate straight, they raise the determinant of the matching MIMO channel. Their closed-form even unitary matrix has rank twice the channel's degrees of freedom, matches optimal value, and runs orders of size faster.
arxiv-2604-09435: Davies, Brown, Gill, and French develop a semi-automated framework to find circumbinary planets in TESS binary curves. Circumbinary planet finds have advanced knowledge of planet birth and motion change, but the group remains small. Their search method removes stellar dips, applies custom cleaning, searches for single transits, and applies auto vetting to filter false alarms. Searching a sample from the TESS Eclipsing Binary list yields one likely event. Tested on known passing circumbinary planets, the method finds at least 50 percent for each, reaching over 75 percent for 9 of 14.
arxiv-2604-09635: Alcalde-Llergo and four colleagues use machine learning to test media literacy among students facing disinformation, focusing on future teachers and media workers. A survey of 723 students in teaching and media programs feeds models that predict media skills and surface key drivers. Complex models beat simpler ones, with school year and prior training lifting forecast accuracy most. The findings point to focused lessons and tailored plans for facing false news online.
arxiv-2604-09935: Gorton and Kravvaris present the first neutron-capture cross section for aluminum-27 with quantified uncertainty, built from shell-model level densities and radiative strength functions. The USDBUQ500 interaction predicts those densities and strength functions with constant uncertainties of 6 and 9 percent. Those uncertainties translate into a 5 to 25 percent uncertainty in the cross section, which shows an oddly non-Gaussian distribution.
arxiv-2604-10335: Ehab and Hamdi describe Adaptive Multi-Expert Reasoning, a scheme that adapts language-model thought to problem hardness. A routing system reads the problem text, predicts hardness and doubt, and guides sampling breadth. Three experts draft tries, refined through fix and final phases. A neural checker checks truth, while grouping-based picking chooses the final answer from accord and quality. On GSM8K, the system scores about 75 percent using only first training data, beating most similar 7B models trained on fake data.
arxiv-2604-10535: Buskila grades small open medical chat models on steadiness, not just scores. A model that shifts answers each time it is asked makes a shaky clinic helper. His open frame runs eight quality checks plus two repeat run steadiness checks. Across three models and 50 MedQuAD items, repeat agreement peaks at one fifth. Worse, 87 to 97 percent of outputs per model come out unique, a gap one shot tests miss.
arxiv-2604-10835: Goodwin and colleagues introduce FOXES, a Vision Transformer method turning spatial ultraviolet views into soft X-ray brightness forecasts for flare sorting. The GOES soft X-ray gauge lacks spatial detail, causing slips like wrong flare sites in busy times, and sees only from Earth orbit. FOXES gives a global 1 to 8 angstrom flux forecast plus per-patch shares showing where light falls. Trained on over 3,200 hours of views, it lands a translational mean absolute error of 0.051 dex for whole-disk totals and splits background flux in flaring and calm times.
arxiv-2604-11135: Fan and five colleagues introduce AIM, an intent-aware world action model with value maps. Pretrained video models provide strong priors for control. Unified models struggle to decode reliable actions without much robot training. The authors blame a mismatch. Video models capture scene evolution, while action generation requires reasoning about location and intent. Instead of decoding actions from visuals, AIM predicts an aligned spatial value map. Built on a pretrained video model, AIM models future observations and value maps. It reaches ninety-four percent average success on RoboTwin 2.0.
arxiv-2604-11235: Dupré relates the homotopy category of pro-p Iwahori-Hecke modules in semisimple rank one to singularity categories of an explicit scheme. For GL2 over a non-archimedean local field, he obtains an equivalence with the singularity category of the Dotto-Emerton-Gee scheme. This recovers Grosse-Klönne's mod-p Langlands correspondence for Hecke modules. The bridge lets results on one side carry over to the other side. He also describes the homotopy categories completely for SL2 and PGL2, with further computations in the GL2 case.
arxiv-2604-11435: Papoudakis, Lapata, and Keller improve character descriptions from books with QA-guided reasoning. Describing book characters demands tracking changing traits, joining scattered clues, and guessing hidden ones. Reasoning models do better here when built-in reasoning is disabled. Their framework splits the steps. The trick is to reason first in Q and A form, then write. A reasoning model produces a structured question-answer trace, and a generation model writes from it. On BookWorm and CroSS, QA-guided reasoning beats strong long-context rivals on faithfulness, detail, and grounding.
arxiv-2604-11735: Braverman and Kazhdan build an analogue of irreducible cuspidal representations for PGL(2) over a 2D local field, swapping the usual base field for a Laurent series field. Up to a small subtlety, their build starts from a quadratic extension and a character that is not Galois invariant. Restricting the new objects to a Borel subgroup keeps them irreducible, yet, unlike the old case, they are not the standard cuspidal object of that subgroup. An appendix sketches a notion of cuspidality for general split reductive groups.
arxiv-2604-11835: Mao and six colleagues tackle tables of data whose layouts differ across sources, an acute problem in clinical medicine. They turn table columns into plain-language statements, then encode them with a pretrained language model. The resulting codes line up across unseen layouts without retraining or manual feature work. Combined with MRI data for dementia diagnosis, the method tops baselines on NACC and ADNI data and beats board-certified neurologists in look-back tests.
arxiv-2604-11935: Bojańczyk, Fabiański, and Stefański settle a higher-order version of an open question about polyregular functions, which map strings to strings. Whether equivalence is decidable for such functions remains open in general. For their higher-order extension, built on a lambda-calculus definition from Bojańczyk, the authors prove equivalence is undecidable by reduction from the tiling problem.
arxiv-2604-12135: Carneiro, Ulhoa, and Maluf trace light rays crossing a sharp gravitational-wave pulse and find the wave leaves a lasting imprint on photon energy. Photons measured by still observers emerge with a finite frequency shift that depends on their path, a memory effect acting straight on the observed redshift. The authors suggest such shifts could explain conflicting readings of supernova redshifts when gravitational radiation lies in between.
arxiv-2604-12335: Rahman and two colleagues propose SynMulti, a single pipeline that auto-generates unlimited multimodal video data with rich labels for training video-understanding models. Real video annotation is costly, slow, and narrow in scope, so the pipeline spans counting, question answering, and segmentation in one system. A question-answering fine-tuning plan pushes models past captions toward deeper visual grounding. Models trained mostly on synthetic data generalize well to real datasets, often beating rivals trained the old way.
arxiv-2604-12635: Leonardo Placidi and three colleagues link qubit connectivity to quantum advantage in noisy IQP circuits. IQP sampling is classically hard in ideal theory. Noise erases that hardness once depth passes a critical threshold. Sparse hardware needs extra routing, deepening compiled circuits. Different graphs thus shift a circuit's place against the simulatability boundary. The team pairs depth estimates with tests on seven device models. Sparse designs tolerate less noise for the same margin. The work tests when experiments stay outside classical simulatability.
arxiv-2604-13035: Sengupta, Ao, and Cascante-Bonilla offer SceneCritic, a rule-based checker for indoor scenes built by language models, replacing judges that score rendered views and wobble with viewpoint and phrasing. Its constraints draw on SceneOnto, a spatial ontology assembled from indoor scene priors, and it checks semantic, orientation, and geometric coherence object by object. In tests SceneCritic tracks human judgment better than vision-language judges, and image-based fixes correct semantics and direction best.
arxiv-2604-13135: Sienicki and Sienicki reply to Schnabel's claimed answer to the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox. It argues a flaw in the EPR implication plus radioactive alpha decay shows predictability allows genuine randomness. They grant the paper is clearly written and tackles an important basic question, but judge its main verdict unfounded. It narrows the original case, leans too hard on Bell-inequality violations, and swaps the central structure of clashing observables and locality logic for simpler correlated random events.
arxiv-2604-13335: Jafari, Berretti, and Basu introduce SEDTalker, a system for speech-driven 3D facial animation that tracks emotion frame by frame. Earlier systems rely on whole-sentence or hand-set emotion labels, but theirs predicts dense emotion types and strengths from speech at each frame. Those signals steer a hybrid Transformer-Mamba animation model, keeping word content apart from emotional style while preserving identity and timing. Tests show strong frame-level emotion recognition, low shape and timing errors, and smooth shifts between expressions.
arxiv-2604-13435: Tokunaga and Nakazato design a silicon-germanium heterostructure for silicon spin qubits with electrons in the L valley of the conduction band. In silicon (111) crystals, strong biaxial tensile strain shifts the band minimum from the delta valley to the L valley. L-valley electrons split into a single ground state and a triply degenerate excited state, low enough for a qubit two-level system. With deformation potential theory and quantum confinement, they find the strain and germanium share for the shift and the critical thickness for plastic relaxation.
arxiv-2604-13835: Rhee and Akinyemi build a compact hybrid CNN-LSTM tool for bean leaf disease classification, aimed at portable devices. Standard convolutional networks struggle with long-range spatial dependencies and carry heavy memory footprints. Adding an LSTM layer models spatial-sequential relationships within feature maps. The hybrid reaches about 94 percent accuracy in a 1.86 megabyte footprint, about 70 percent smaller than traditional convolutional systems. Tailored image augmentation beats generic combinations at preserving diagnostic patterns, and on the ibean dataset the EfficientNet-B7 plus LSTM variant reaches an F1 score of about 99 percent.
arxiv-2604-14535: Yoshida and Meier show that active galactic nuclei found by the James Webb Space Telescope at redshifts above five could source ultrahigh-energy cosmogenic neutrinos. If those nuclei emit ultrahigh-energy protons, neutrino production in the high-redshift cosmic microwave background yields a flux bump near 50 PeV. That flux may match IceCube's current intensity estimate within the luminosity and number-density range allowed by Webb data. Future observations confirming the 50-PeV bump and constraining small-scale anisotropy would pin down early-universe cosmic-ray emissions.
arxiv-2604-14735: Xiang, Chang, Fang, and Zhang present the first study of a rare Dalitz decay in which an excited kaon, K-star-892, sheds a virtual photon that becomes an electron or muon pair. Using a single-pole model for the transition form factor, they predict its rate and pair-mass spread. The same spectrum could hide a light dark photon as a narrow bump. Their results set up the decay as a fresh probe of meson structure and dark-sector physics, with BESIII well placed to test it.
arxiv-2604-14935: Sharma, Manoj Mishra, and Devendra Mishra propose Z-4n-detection for quantum LiDAR, where the detector clicks only when photon counts equal four times a whole number, with all other counts treated as no-click. Using a superposition of four coherent states plus vacuum as input, they test a Mach-Zehnder interferometer design. Against the standard Z-detection scheme, which clicks for any photon number, the new scheme significantly enhances resolution and broadens the working point for phase sensitivity. The findings point toward more accurate and sensitive quantum LiDAR measurement.
arxiv-2604-15035: Bonfanti and colleagues map a five-planet family around the star TOI-5624. Space telescopes caught four smaller Neptune-like worlds crossing the star, with orbits lasting about three to twenty-two days. Timing shifts in the outermost world point to a fifth planet that never crosses the star, moving in near two-to-one step with it. The sizes and weights are fixed with rare sharpness, a feat matched before only by the TRAPPIST-1 family.
arxiv-2604-15135: Shah and Urschel pin down the exact exponential rate at which square Fourier submatrices grow ill-conditioned. Though the full Fourier matrix is unitary, its submatrices can grow sharply ill-conditioned, blocking accurate computation. For rows and columns in one block they resolve the rate exactly, yielding a tight upper bound tied to Catalan's constant for contiguous columns. The analysis extends to Vandermonde-like matrices through log potentials.
arxiv-2604-15235: Peng and colleagues build a primal bootstrap method for effective field theories with a graviton pole. Using finite-resolution sampling instead of smearing, with direct control over subtraction counts, they reproduce known projective bounds in six or more dimensions and tighten them in five. The method also imposes linearized unitarity directly and opens access to extremal spectra. Applied to crossing-symmetric dispersion relations, it yields new non-projective bounds fixing the overall scale of couplings, showing the cutoff cannot sit far above the Planck scale.
arxiv-2604-15435: Burke and McGoldrick show that quantum search keeps its quadratic speedup even with the oracle as the sole global operator and all other steps acting locally on separate partitions. Their recursive construction gives an exact closed-form dynamics when initial and target states factor across partitions. On an 18-qubit problem, two-stage partitioning cuts non-oracle circuit depth by 51 to 96 percent at the cost of up to 9 percent more oracle calls.
arxiv-2604-15535: Khiste, Tarte, and Joshi prove the third conjecture of Bender and colleagues on complemented zero-divisor graphs of semigroups. They settle it positively after the first two fell to counterexamples. The claim concerns a graph G(S) that is uniquely complemented, has clique number 3 or more, and gives every vertex a unique complement. Such a graph matches the power-set graph on n elements, where n is the clique number.
arxiv-2604-15735: Wang and seven colleagues fuse sketch lines and text cues for fine-grained image hunt. Sketches give shape but no color or feel, while text gives color and feel but no shape. A step-by-step toughening pass hardens the model for shaky asks, a class-knowledge pass tunes the space, and a multi-stage cross-mode match lines up traits across modes. Their new STBIR test set backs the work, and trials beat past best methods by a wide mark.
arxiv-2604-16035: Cabral, Evangelista, and Santos study the Coulomb potential in Podolsky-Carroll-Field-Jackiw electrodynamics. Podolsky theory extends Maxwell theory with a higher-derivative term that alters photon dispersion and tames divergences. Coupling it to the Carroll-Field-Jackiw model adds a Lorentz-violating background vector. In the combined framework, the photon propagator applied to Möller scattering shows the CFJ term can bring back the divergence it suppresses. In the slow-motion limit, spatial and timelike components both matter for the potential, the spatial part breaking isotropy.
arxiv-2604-16235: Kim and Kim test many-language large language models adapted for Korean-centred tasks by token pruning. Pruning drops tokens and embeddings for languages irrelevant to the target use. They test Aya, Qwen3, Gemma-3, and Llama-3 across original, English-Korean, and English-Korean-Chinese vocabularies. Pruning improves steady output by cutting language confusion. It often lifts machine translation on Korean-specific tasks, though following instructions varies by design.
arxiv-2604-16535: Shyamal and colleagues improve test-time scaling, where models generate many answers and pick the best. Learned scorers are strong but costly, while cheap confidence heuristics often perform much worse. SCATR trains a lightweight scorer on a small calibration set from hidden base-model representations. Across coding and math benchmarks, it beat confidence baselines by up to 9 percent. It matched LoRA fine-tuning on the same data with 8,000 times fewer trainable parameters. It also rivalled strong reward-model baselines while running far faster.
arxiv-2604-16735: Avis and Devroye compare cut, metric, rooted metric polytopes and the elliptope. After a change, the cut polytope sits inside the other three as polynomial-time relaxations. Volume ratios bound tightness globally, beyond worst-case ratios for non-negative coefficients. For large n, the rooted metric polytope over the complete graph exceeds the elliptope. The metric polytope is smaller for small n but larger for large n, crossover near n equal to 13. Exact formulas cover sparse cut families, including every cycle elliptope, whose cut ratio converges rapidly to one.
arxiv-2604-17035: Davis takes on a puzzle in superstatistics, a scheme for systems in non-equilibrium steady states such as collisionless plasmas and gravity-bound systems. The inverse-temperature spread cannot be measured, since its uncertainty does not come from fluctuations of a phase-space function. He shows a mapping between functions of the superstatistical temperature and functions of the fundamental temperature, a model-dependent function of energy, whose average values coincide.
arxiv-2604-17235: Gao and four colleagues build a hybrid benchmark dataset for seismic reading of global shelf-edge clinothems, combining 3,000 unlabeled field records with 4,000 labeled synthetic records made by forward models. Traditional reading is slow and highly subjective, while AI work has stalled for lack of broad, representative benchmarks. Baseline deep learning models tested on the sets give strong results, showing the set supports model training, scoring, and practical use. The set is released to advance deep learning for seismic reading.
arxiv-2604-17335: Zhang and nine colleagues teach a humanoid robot to walk whole-body style over rough ground. A diffusion model predicts terrain-aware reference motion, and a separate tracker learns to follow it. A final closed-loop fine-tuning round hardens the tracker against imperfect predictions. The system runs on a Unitree G1 robot using only onboard sensing and computing, and hardware trials crossed boxes, hurdles, stairs, and mixed ground.
arxiv-2604-17635: Zheng, Papka, and Lan present EcoShift, a performance-aware framework for cluster-wide power management on power-capped heterogeneous systems. Old policies lean on fair-share or use heuristics and miss how applications respond to CPU and GPU power caps, wasting reclaimed power. EcoShift pairs online prediction with a dynamic-programming allocator that distributes reclaimed power across CPU-GPU applications for peak average gain. Emulation on Intel CPU and NVIDIA A100/H100 GPU platforms shows up to 6 percent average gain over rival policies while preserving the cluster-wide power cap.
arxiv-2604-17835: Liang Li studies twenty single-pulse gamma-ray bursts detected by Fermi whose spectra track intensity, splitting a familiar pattern into three subclasses. Type I, five bursts, shows spectral peak and flux peaking together. Type II, thirteen bursts, has the spectral peak first and dominates the sample. Type III, two bursts, peaks after flux. Type II bursts run harder and show broader flux pulses. They more often show lopsided rising and falling branches, fitting nonthermal or hybrid emission better than tightly coupled evolution.
arxiv-2604-18235: Wu and eight colleagues fix a flaw in GRPO training for search agents that answer questions over several search rounds. Correct middle steps get punished when the final answer is wrong, and training often turns unstable or collapses. Their CalibAdv method scales down outsized negative advantages using middle-step correctness, then rebalances positive and negative advantages. Tests across three models and seven benchmarks show better performance and steadier training, with a lightweight design built from standard rollout signals.
arxiv-2604-18535: Ho constructs dyadic lacunary counterexamples for two Erdős problems about circle dilates. The key tool is a dyadic spike block: rare spikes create long positive runs in lacunary averages, while a deterministic floor blocks cancellation from later stages. The construction gives a mean-zero function integrable to every finite power, with doubling dilates, whose averages blow up almost everywhere. Thus a positive theorem above one-half cannot extend to one-half, answering Problem 996 negatively, while a second choice answers Problem 995 for every finite exponent from 2 upward.
arxiv-2604-18635: Griffith offers four principled gauges of integration built on the partial information decomposition frame, in aid of the math behind the Information Integration Theory of Consciousness. He sets them beside present IIT practice in plain deterministic nets. His gauges are the first IIT-linked, state-tied integration gauges to meet standard info-theoretic floor and ceiling bounds on their own. Like IIT4, the four are non-Shannon, yet outside IIT they match standard Shannon-based irreducibility gauges in discrete dynamical systems.
arxiv-2604-18735: Gustafsson and three colleagues map magnetic fields in the interacting Abell 3391-3395 cluster system using wide-field MeerKAT polarimetry. From a dense grid of Faraday rotation measures for polarized background sources, they identify 434 polarized sources in the field.
